title: Melanoma
subtitle: Staged by Breslow thickness + ulceration; LDH is a staging modifier in M1 disease · ~50% of cutaneous melanomas carry BRAF V600 · the central modern question is immunotherapy sequencing, not whether to give it
source: Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Melanoma — an advanced-disease chapter. Biopsy technique, excision margins, SLNB indications, dosing, surveillance and the variant/toxicity material are not in it; those are marked † and drawn from NCCN and product labeling.

blocks.heading: Workup
items: † Excisional biopsy with 1–3 mm margins, full thickness, oriented along lymphatic drainage — avoid a superficial shave, which compromises Breslow depth
Pathologic confirmation; report Breslow thickness and ulceration († mitotic rate is still reported though no longer a staging criterion)
Imaging: CT chest/abdomen/pelvis (add neck if head-and-neck primary), or PET/CT
BRAF V600 testing in all advanced cutaneous melanoma
If BRAF wild-type → NGS; in acral/mucosal look specifically for KIT mutations or TRK fusions

blocks.heading: Staging — AJCC 8th
rows: T1 ≤1 mm · T2 >1–2 · T3 >2–4 · T4 >4 mm; suffix a = no ulceration, b = ulcerated
T1a = <0.8 mm without ulceration; T1b = <0.8 mm ulcerated, or 0.8–1.0 mm either way
N1 = 1 node or in-transit/satellite alone · N2 = 2–3 · N3 = ≥4, or matted
M1a skin/soft tissue/non-regional node · M1b lung · M1c other visceral · M1d = CNS

blocks.heading: † Localized management (NCCN)
blocks.footnote: † Sentinel lymph node biopsy: not recommended for T1a (risk <5%) · discuss for T1b · recommended for T2 and above. Completion lymph node dissection is no longer routine after a positive sentinel node (MSLT-II, DeCOG-SLT) — nodal ultrasound surveillance instead.

boxes: wide local excision by Breslow depth
† BRAF V600: dabrafenib + trametinib an option
improves EFS vs adjuvant therapy alone
anti-PD-1 alone if not fit for a combination
brain mets → brief BRAF/MEK then switch (sandwich)
for systemic therapy — give adjuvant therapy
symptomatic or on steroids: RR only ~17%
→ add surgery + targeted therapy; SRS, not WBRT

blocks.heading: Regimens & dosing
rows: † ipilimumab 3 mg/kg + nivolumab 1 mg/kg q3wk ×4, then nivolumab maintenance
resect → expand ex vivo with IL-2 → lymphodepleting chemo → single infusion → high-dose IL-2
largely replaced by checkpoint and targeted therapy
blocks.footnote: † Doses are from product labeling — the handbook chapter states dosing only for the two neoadjuvant regimens. Cytotoxic chemotherapy “no longer plays a well-defined role” in metastatic melanoma.

blocks.heading: Biomarker → therapy
rows: BRAF + MEK doublet — always dual, never single-agent BRAF (resistance, and BRAFi skin toxicity). Immunotherapy still works and generally comes first
Imatinib — responses with activating mutations (~1/3 respond); KIT amplification alone typically does not respond
Found on NGS in BRAF wild-type acral/mucosal disease
Tebentafusp in metastatic uveal melanoma; also eligibility for brenetafusp trials in cutaneous disease
Send NGS for other actionable drivers

pages.subtitle: Page 2 — trial evidence, staging detail, immune toxicity and variants

blocks.heading: Trial evidence
rows: ipi/nivo vs nivo vs ipi — median OS 72 / 37 / 20 months; 10-yr OS 43% / 37% / 19%. If progression-free at 3 years, 10-yr melanoma-specific survival >96% (Wolchok, NEJM 2024)
brain metastases on ipi/nivo — asymptomatic: intracranial ORR 53–57%, 36-mo iPFS ~54%, OS ~72%. Symptomatic or on steroids: RR ~17%, iPFS ~19%, OS ~37% (Long, JCO 2023)
relatlimab + nivolumab vs nivolumab — median PFS 10.1 vs 4.6 months (Tawbi, NEJM 2022)
neoadjuvant ipi/nivo → adjuvant nivolumab — EFS and distant-metastasis-free survival benefit; major pathologic response 58%; grade 3+ AEs ~30% (Rozeman, Nat Med 2024)
neoadjuvant → adjuvant pembrolizumab — 2-yr EFS 72% vs 48% with adjuvant alone; no added surgical complications (Patel, NEJM 2023)
BRAF V600: IO first then targeted vs the reverse — 2-yr OS 72% vs 52% (Atkins, JCO 2023)
at 4 years, IO-first or sandwich beats targeted-first for PFS and OS (Ascierto, JCO 2023)
pooled phase III: 34% alive at 5 years, ~20% progression-free; better with normal LDH, good performance status, <3 metastatic sites
RR ~30% with durable remissions; superior to ipilimumab in PD-1-refractory disease (Warner, Clin Cancer Res 2022)

blocks.heading: † Adjuvant trials
rows: nivolumab 480 mg q4wk × 12 months, resected stage IIB/IIC — RFS HR 0.42, DMFS HR 0.47
nivolumab vs ipilimumab, resected stage IIIB/C–IV
dabrafenib + trametinib × 12 months, resected stage III BRAF V600
blocks.footnote: All are 1-year regimens. The stage IIB/IIC trials have shown RFS and DMFS benefit but no definitive OS benefit yet — worth saying out loud when consenting a patient with resected node-negative disease.

blocks.heading: Stage groupings
rows: 0 Tis · IA T1a · IB T1b or T2a · IIA T2b/T3a · IIB T3b/T4a · IIC T4b · III = any N ≥N1, M0 · IV = M1
T0 with N1b/c · T1a–T2a with N1b/c or N2b · T2b/T3a with N1a–c or N2a/b
T0 with N2b/c or N3b/c · T1a–T3a with N2c or N3a–c · T3b/T4a with any N ≥N1 · T4b with N1a–N2c
a = clinically occult (found on SLNB) · b = clinically detected · c = in-transit, satellite or microsatellite disease present

blocks.heading: † Immune-related adverse events
items: Grade 1: usually continue with close monitoring. Grade 2: hold the checkpoint inhibitor; prednisone 0.5–1 mg/kg/day if persistent
Grade 3–4: hold or permanently discontinue; prednisone or methylprednisolone 1–2 mg/kg/day, tapered over at least 4–6 weeks
Steroid-refractory colitis → infliximab or vedolizumab. Hepatitis → mycophenolate, not infliximab (hepatotoxicity)
Myocarditis → urgent high-dose steroids and permanent discontinuation — rare but highly lethal

Endocrine events are the exception: hypophysitis, thyroiditis, adrenal insufficiency and type 1 diabetes are usually irreversible, but you replace the hormone and generally continue the checkpoint inhibitor
Monitor TSH and free T4 at baseline and every 4–6 weeks; check HBsAg and HBcAb before starting
Onset is typically weeks to months — but can occur after discontinuation. Ipilimumab-containing regimens carry the highest risk

blocks.heading: Variants & special situations
rows: More common in darker skin. Lower TMB, lower BRAF rate, lower immunotherapy response, more aggressive — check KIT
Distinct genetics, low BRAF, poor immunotherapy response, presents late because the site is hidden; KIT actionable

Biologically distinct; metastasizes to liver first. Localized: plaque radiation or enucleation. Metastatic: liver-directed therapy (HAI, TACE, radioembolization, ablation); † tebentafusp if HLA-A*02:01
Usually BRAF wild-type with very high TMB — unusually responsive to anti-PD-1. SLNB value is debated in pure desmoplastic disease
Margin assessment is difficult (subclinical extension); imiquimod or radiation if not a surgical candidate
Isolated limb infusion or perfusion, T-VEC, intralesional therapy, or systemic therapy
Treat by stage as though cutaneous — outcomes are similar or better

blocks.heading: † Surveillance (NCCN)
items: Stage IA–IIA: H&P q6–12 months × 5 years, then annually; no routine imaging
Stage IIB–IV: H&P q3–6 months × 2 years, then q3–12 months × 3 years; imaging q3–12 months for 2–3 years
Annual skin examination for life, plus education on skin self-examination and sun protection

Pseudoprogression: immunotherapy responses can be slow with transient worsening before shrinkage — especially with ipilimumab-containing regimens. † iRECIST requires confirmatory imaging before calling progression

blocks.heading: † Hereditary predisposition
rows: Familial melanoma — also confers pancreatic cancer risk
Uveal melanoma, mesothelioma, renal cell carcinoma, cutaneous melanocytic tumors
Red hair and fair skin phenotype; modest risk modifier
